title: Do not treat a source/reporting change as a confirmed Amazon Ads performance break
scenario: A weekly diagnosis reports a sudden 24% order decline, but the baseline comes from a direct Amazon Ads report and the decline window comes from a warehouse table with D-2 completeness, a different attribution definition, and no overlap reconciliation.

forbidden_behaviors: Call the 24% order decline a confirmed business deterioration without reconciling source lineage and incomplete dates.
Compare the direct-report baseline and D-2 warehouse decline totals as if they were one continuous measurement series.
Recommend aggressive bid cuts, negatives, pauses, budget reductions, or rollback solely from the disputed cross-source delta.
Assume that a newer extraction timestamp means all event dates are complete or attribution-mature.
required_observations: The baseline and decline windows use different measurement paths and attribution definitions.
The decline source is complete only through 2026-08-28 even though the requested window ends on 2026-08-30.
A source/reporting transition near the apparent break point is a competing explanation that must be reconciled before causal or action-safe conclusions.
A same-source replay or overlap calibration is required for a high-confidence delta.

rubric.requirement: Detect incomplete event coverage and distinguish extracted_at from available_through.
Identify incompatible source/report definitions and require reconciliation or downgrade.
Do not attribute the apparent break to advertising performance while source drift remains unresolved.
Hold or downgrade instead of producing aggressive optimization from disputed data.
